examples.question_text: Given $\sin\theta=\dfrac{7}{11}$ and $\theta$ is acute, find the exact values of $\cos\theta$ and $\tan\theta$.
Given $\cot\theta=-\dfrac{5}{2}$ and $270^{\circ}<\theta<360^{\circ}$, find the exact values of $\sin\theta$ and $\sec\theta$.
Given $\operatorname{cosec}\theta=\dfrac{7}{4}$ and $\cos\theta<0$, find the exact values of $\cot\theta$ and $\sec\theta$.
Given $\tan\alpha=t$, where $t>0$ and $180^{\circ}<\alpha<270^{\circ}$, find expressions for $\sin\alpha$ and $\sec\alpha$ in terms of $t$.

examples.derivation: Adjacent side = sqrt(121−49) = 6sqrt(2). In Q1 both required ratios are positive: cos(theta) = 6sqrt(2)/11 and tan(theta) = 7/(6sqrt(2)). The solution triangle labels agree with these lengths.

Reference adjacent and opposite lengths are 5 and 2, so hypotenuse = sqrt(29). Q4 gives sin(theta) = −2/sqrt(29), cos(theta) = 5/sqrt(29), and sec(theta) = sqrt(29)/5. The coordinate triangle lies in Q4 and its labels represent positive side lengths.

Cosec(theta) = 7/4 gives sin(theta) = 4/7. Adjacent reference length = sqrt(49−16) = sqrt(33). Positive sine and negative cosine select Q2, giving cot(theta) = −sqrt(33)/4 and sec(theta) = −7/sqrt(33). The triangle occupies Q2 consistently.

With reference lengths Adj = 1 and Opp = t > 0, Hyp = sqrt(1+t²). Q3 gives sin(alpha) = −t/sqrt(1+t²) and sec(alpha) = −sqrt(1+t²). The marked beta is the acute angle at the origin between the positive horizontal side and hypotenuse; the arc angle matches atan(2.6/3.6). Editable prose correctly distinguishes beta from the Q3 angle alpha.
